checks.invariant: A less-trusted other app on the same OS profile cannot read the remembered staff password from SecureStore.
checks.result: Writes go only through expo-secure-store. app.json has no keychain-access-groups, no android.sharedUserId, and no exported provider. Other apps are not granted that read in source. Same-app reads after sign-in (silentRefresh, boot restore) are the intended OS principal and are not a boundary violation.

checks.invariant: The reusable staff password is not persisted in an OS credential item that is backup-eligible or readable without user presence, unless a refresh token is used instead.
checks.result: Every successful signIn stores JSON {email, password} under ct_mobile_login_credentials via loginWithPassword. STORE_OPTS sets only keychainAccessible AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK (not AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY). requireAuthentication is never passed on set or get. getItemAsync is called with the key only. The JWT is stored the same way. There is no remember-me opt-out on the login screen.

checks.invariant: Android allowBackup and iOS ThisDeviceOnly / merged packaging actually prevent a backup or other-profile reader from recovering the password.
checks.result: No android/ or ios/ trees exist (EAS managed builds in eas.json). app.json android block does not set allowBackup. plugins lists expo-secure-store as a bare string with no configureAndroidBackup. iOS AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK is the backup-eligible Keychain class; ThisDeviceOnly is unused. Whether Google Auto Backup, Finder/iCloud encrypted backup, MDM, or another OS user/work profile can read the shipped item is an OS/packaging fact.

checks.invariant: In-app sign-out and account switch do not leave the remembered password for a later Estate-EZ session on this install.
checks.result: signOut deletes ct_mobile_access_token, ct_mobile_login_credentials, and the selected-sale keys. Failed loadAccount after signIn also deletes credentials. The next in-app login cannot read the previous password from SecureStore. ct_capture.db lot drafts are not wiped; that is leftover queue data on the same OS profile, not a password reader.

candidates.title: Remembered staff password stored in backup-eligible SecureStore
candidates.description: A backup or other-OS-profile restorer—not another app on the live profile—may recover the reusable Estate-EZ password. Each mobile sign-in writes email+password under ct_mobile_login_credentials with iOS AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK and without requireAuthentication. That item can mint a new staff JWT via silent re-login. Same-app use on the signed-in OS user is out of scope.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: loginWithPassword persists the raw password in expo-secure-store using AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK rather than a ThisDeviceOnly accessibility class or a refresh token, and app.json neither disables Android allowBackup nor pins SecureStore backup rules.

trace.description: After POST /auth/login, the app writes JSON {email, password} to SecureStore key ct_mobile_login_credentials with no remember-me flag.
All secureSet calls, including the password, use AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK and do not set requireAuthentication or a ThisDeviceOnly constant.
The password string is stored in the OS keychain/keystore-backed store. Boot and silentRefresh later read it with getItemAsync(key) and call login again.

evidence.description: CREDENTIALS_KEY is ct_mobile_login_credentials, documented as email+password for silent re-login when the JWT expires.
Stored value is JSON.stringify({ email, password }) of the staff password, not a refresh token.
keychainAccessible is AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK, which is backup-eligible on iOS; AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY is not used.
secureGet calls getItemAsync(key) with no requireAuthentication options.
android package com.caringtransitions.capture sets no allowBackup false and no backup/dataExtraction rules.
plugins includes expo-secure-store as a string with no configureAndroidBackup object.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox and parent artifact promotion unavailable
No android/ or ios/ trees; EAS merged AndroidManifest allowBackup plus SecureStore backup XML, and the shipped IPA keychain accessibility, are packaging facts
Encrypted iCloud/Finder/Google/MDM backup restore of dummy ct_mobile_login_credentials onto a second dummy device or OS profile was not observed

validation_plan.local: On an isolated simulator/emulator with a dummy tenant, sign in, then read the written item's iOS accessibility class and Android backup XML/EncryptedSharedPreferences binding. Restore an encrypted backup onto a second dummy device or profile and see whether the dummy password silently logs in. Do not use live staff accounts.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects the EAS production APK/IPA AndroidManifest allowBackup and expo-secure-store backup rules, and the iOS keychain accessibility for com.caringtransitions.capture. Do not export or replay live staff passwords.

hardening: Replace remembered password with a server refresh token so SecureStore never holds the staff password.
If background access after lock is required, use AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY so iOS backups omit the item.
requireAuthentication is a same-device presence gate; it does not stop backup restore and is not a substitute for ThisDeviceOnly or a refresh token.
Set android.allowBackup false or pass expo-secure-store configureAndroidBackup explicitly in app.json so EAS prebuild cannot drop exclusion XML.
signOut deletes the SecureStore password but leaves ct_capture.db drafts on the same OS profile; wipe or rebind that queue if shared-phone staff switching is in scope.
